items.confound_note: All four cases are one year group at one school inside a single autumn term, so they share one policy and illness history. The borough-wide reward scheme launched at Brackhill Academy that term, and the decade-low local illness rates, each cover every case at once. Because each cohort is compared only against itself a term earlier, when neither the scheme nor the mild illness season applied, nothing in the register separates those causes from the timetable change.

items.confound_note: All four cases measure lateness, not absence. A lateness mark is entered against a pupil who turned up and was registered present for the session, so the register counts lateness and absence as separate quantities. Moving the start of the school day can cut lateness in every cohort while the number of sessions missed altogether holds flat or rises. The claim is about absence, so none of the four cases speaks to it.
items.notes: Closer is verbatim identical to both TRUE items; the only change from diverse_true is the measured-quantity word, absence to lateness, in all four cases. Check that lateness reads as genuinely non-equivalent to absence and that nothing in the passage flags the swap. A shared confound is unavailable here because the four cohorts span four schools, four year groups, four terms and four registrars.
